title: Never Again: Online Replication of the Fading Affect Bias in the Context of Alcohol During the COVID-19 Pandemic
content: The Fading Affect Bias (FAB) is the faster fading of unpleasant than pleasant affect for autobiographical events, which seems to be a healthy coping mechanism/outcome, as it is positively related to healthy/adaptive variables (e.g., grit) and negatively related to unhealthy/non-adaptive variables (e.g., depression). Past research showed that alcohol consumption was positively related to FAB for alcohol events and negatively related to FAB for non-alcohol events. The current study replicated the previous study during the COVID-19 pandemic using an online procedure. We replicated past research, finding that the FAB was positively related to healthy outcomes (e.g., rehearsal, positive PANAS, spirituality, positive religious coping, religiosity, Brief Cope, and grit) and negatively related to healthy outcomes (negative religious coping and negative PANAS). Surprisingly, the FAB was also positively related to non-adaptive alcohol outcomes. Furthermore, the FAB was larger for alcohol than non-alcohol events at low levels of spirituality, positive PANAS, and positive religious coping for non-alcohol events, and the FAB was larger for non-alcohol than alcohol events at high levels of the 3 continuous variables. These expected and surprising results were discussed.
